hook.text: After 9/11, nearly 3,000 people died. Many remains were fragments. DNA became the primary identification tool.

buildup.text: Over 20,000 body fragments were recovered. Heat, fire, and jet fuel had severely degraded most genetic material.

discovery.text: New DNA extraction methods were developed specifically for this case. SNP analysis supplemented standard STR work.

twist.text: By 2024, only 60% of victims were identified. Some fragments are still being tested with improving technology.

climax.text: Families waited decades for a name. Each identification brought closure—one fragment, one family at a time.

punchline.text: The science keeps advancing. The families keep waiting.

quiz.question: Why was DNA identification of 9/11 victims so difficult?
